newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks correct, stay above 1000 level.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks correct, stay above 1000 level.

text.p: Greek shares corrected on Friday but managed to settle above 1,000 points on the benchmark index with market watchers expecting buying interest to continue as dividend yields and trading multiples were attractive.

"On Friday we saw the market correct after it had risen in the previous two sessions. People are feeling confident now as the Delta Securities scandal seems to be left behind and stock prices are attractive," said broker Geli Petroulaki at Ergo Securities.
November wholesale price inflation fell to 5.0 percent year-on-year from 6.1 percent in October, the National Statistics Service announced on Friday.
The Athens general share index closed down 0.36 percent or 3.66 points at 1008.73 from Thursday's 1012.39, after it had opened at 1009.78.
Shares of Intrasoft rose to 1,750, gaining 50 drachmas, on news it signed a four-year deal worth 3.4 billion drachmas with the informatics directorate of the EU Commission.
Banks lost 0.21 percent, construction gained 0.34 percent while small caps rose by 0.07 percent. Industrials closed 0.44 percent lower while investment shares rose by 0.29 percent.

"The construction sector did not do too well in 1996. Share prices had fallen quite significantly and their recovery is considered normal," said John Marcopoulos, managing director of Sigma Securities.
He added that 1997 will be a better year for construction stocks, saying that Michaniki's price had been low for some time and was a good buy.
Friday's turnover fell to 7.8 billion drachmas on volume of 3.1 million shares. Losers led gainers 116 to 93 with 28 issues unchanged on 237 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 777.00-795.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, dropped 40 drachmas to 4,900.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.81-$12.81. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,859-5,179 drachmas. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
